brief.name: mixed-projection-v1
brief.hypothesis: One packed target projection pass can amortize weight reads across independent prefill and verification rows on GB10.
brief.timing: Three reversed-order ABBA repetitions, five graph replays per sample; all 64 layers, separate full prefill then verify sweeps versus packed per-layer sweeps. Includes torch.cat and output split views; no state/attention work.
brief.numerical_gate: Every operation and each prefill/verify partition finite with relative RMS error <= 0.01 against separate execution. Diagnostic only: full target oracle, EOS/cache/seeded sampling and quality gates still required.
brief.prototype_gate: At least 10% reduction of a named dense family at a prefill size <= 512, passing the numerical gate. Independent confirmation required; this is not an HTTP speed claim.
brief.promotion_gate: local-v1 selected completion >= 10% better, protected regression <= 5%, full correctness and quality, equal memory and independent repetitions. No default change from this profile.
brief.limitations: Captured activation replay excludes cross-layer dependencies, attention, GDN state, draft generation, logits and commits. Logical weight bytes are not measured DRAM traffic. Three repetitions are a pilot; no tail percentiles or statistical claim.

capture.prefill: First 2048 rows of cold local-v1 session; smaller shapes use prefix slices.
capture.verify: One eager k=7 B=3 round after coding/chat/json prefill; B=1 uses first eight rows.

profile.http: First-pilot raw HTTP preserved in proof directory; grading included terminal tokens incorrectly. See v2 amendment.

brief.v2_amendment: Account for current B=3 graph padding to B=4; separate verification executes 32 rows while packed uses 24 active rows. Add the observed 124-row session tail at prefix 2048. Gates unchanged. HTTP text removes the same terminal IDs as local-v1 before grading.

capture.prefill: First 2048 rows of cold local-v1 session; smaller shapes use prefix slices.
capture.verify: Eager replay of exact graph inputs for k=7 B=3 padded to B=4, before acceptance; first 24 rows active, final eight dummy. B=1 probes use the first eight rows.
capture.tail: Final 124 session rows after the first 2048 are committed; paged prefix attention.

requests.text: Prefix caching allows the local model to reuse previously computed attention states for the shared context, such as system prompts or earlier parts of the codebase. This significantly reduces the computational overhead and latency for subsequent requests, enabling faster response times. Consequently, the coding assistant can provide more immediate feedback and maintain a smoother interactive experience for the user.

quality.rubric: Explain reuse of the shared prompt computation; do not claim generated answers are cached.

requests.text: Rollback marks a request uncacheable because in-place kernel writes may have corrupted the recurrent state slot during the failed forward pass. Since the state no longer accurately represents the committed prefix, caching it would introduce invalid data into the radix cache. This ensures that subsequent requests do not reuse a slot containing inconsistent or damaged recurrent state.

quality.rubric: Identify that freeing reserved pages cannot undo partially mutated recurrent state; poisoned state must not become a reusable cache entry.
